cohort: The participants were 578 patients who underwent caesarean sections, divided into two equal groups based on whether they received continuous or intermittent rectus sheath closure.
finding: Intermittent suturing of the rectus sheath resulted in a lower incidence of surgical site infection and fewer clinical manifestations (induration, pain, serous discharge, spontaneous superficial dehiscence) compared to continuous suturing in caesarean section patients.
